chapter_seo_title: Han Li’s Settlement on Kui Xing Island – The Immortal Ascension Pavilion
chapter_meta_description: Han Li arrives at Kui Xing Island’s gate to reality: a crumbling Immortal Ascension Pavilion with a luxurious interior and a grumpy senior who knows exactly who he is.
og_title: Han Li Faces a Grumpy Senior and a Five-Year Duel on Kui Xing Island
og_description: The new island has new rules—including a surprise sparring match with the senior’s own defeated disciple.
twitter_title: Paperwork, Pearls, and a Five-Year Promise – Han Li’s First Day on Kui Xing Island
twitter_description: Han Li learns the island’s power structure and agrees to a future duel he might not be able to win.

lore_anchors.definition: The administrative office for settlement, land registration, and token management on Kui Xing Island; its decrepit exterior masks an opulent interior.
The institutionalized hired security force whose members serve as temporary fighters for wealthy island families.
A decennial tournament on Green Cloud Mountain where the thirty-six richest peaks are contested in direct combat.
The point of densest spiritual qi on a given landmass, often claimed by the island’s most powerful cultivator as a personal cultivation site.
The third major cultivation realm, conferring greatly increased lifespan and magical power; a standard measure of a strong regional cultivator.
A low-grade magic tool issued to registered settlers on Kui Xing Island, granting a minor water-repelling effect.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is the Immortal Ascension Pavilion so shabby on the outside?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It is a deliberate psychological display: the owner hides his wealth behind a broken facade to signal that he is both unpredictable and not to be underestimated.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li agree to the five-year duel so quickly?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He assesses it as a deferred cost—agreeing avoids immediate conflict and buys him time to grow stronger, which is his default tactical position.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What does the senior’s coughing mean?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It signals that even a late Foundation Establishment cultivator is still mortal; his finite lifespan and declining health are an undercurrent of tension in the chapter.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Can Qi Condensation cultivators get their own mountain?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Not on Green Cloud Mountain. Foundation Establishment cultivators are entitled to a peak, while Qi Condensation cultivators must settle for valleys or caves.
